summary.headline: Refex Q1 FY27 standalone continuing revenue rose 76% YoY to INR619 crore, with EBITDA of INR105 crore (17% margin) and PAT of INR73.6 crore (+123%).
summary.overview: Standalone continuing-operations revenue grew 76% YoY to INR619 crore and EBITDA rose to INR105 crore at a 17% margin, while PAT reached INR73.6 crore (11.9% margin). Ash and coal handling remained the largest contributor despite acute diesel shortages and logistics disruptions linked to geopolitical developments. Wind turbine execution started contributing INR295 crore in the quarter at near-zero margin, and the mobility demerger is progressing toward a shareholder meeting next month.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time bank processing charges (loan takeover by Indian Overseas Bank)

segments.name: Ash and coal handling
segments.commentary: Largest contributor to revenue and profit; volume run rate of 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1, with management targeting close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (some remarks cited 75,000-80,000 by Q4). Q2 expected to be slower, Q3-Q4 to scale up. Management guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%.

segments.name: Wind energy
segments.commentary: Q1 execution INR295 crore at near-zero margin; order book INR1,860 crore of which INR525 crore executed and INR1,300 crore remaining. FY27 execution guided at INR1,700-1,800 crore with 5-6% net margin targeted by year-end. Operates as a product supplier (turbine, tower, blades) with a 76-77% stake in the JV.

segments.name: Mobility (Refex Mobility)
segments.commentary: Asset-light premium corporate mobility; being demerged into a separate listed company. NCLT has approved convening shareholder and creditor meetings, with equity shareholder meeting scheduled for next month. Expected to exit discontinued operations by end of Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas
segments.commentary: Fully discontinued as of the last quarter; part of discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: Ash and coal handling run rate to reach close to 90,000 tonnes per day in Q4 FY27; Q2 to be slower, Q3-Q4 to pick up; management says the core business will maintain a CAGR at least as good as last year's (~28%).
Wind FY27 execution of INR1,700-1,800 crore; net margin 5-6% by end of FY27 and profitability by year-end; Q3-Q4 margins expected to improve as unbilled material gets billed.
Wind localisation: management expects about 85% of components localised within 12 months, with margins similar to the core business in about 2 years; blades to be made in-house.
Mobility demerger expected to be completed with discontinued operations gone by end of Q3 FY27.
Wind orders in advanced closure expected within 30-60 days; new orders would spill over into FY28.
capex_capacity: Silvassa wind assembly plant is leased; capex to date limited to about INR3.5-4 crore of repairs and maintenance; rated capacity about 1 GW, which management equates to roughly INR5,000-6,000 crore of revenue.
First 5.3 MW turbine erected by a customer at Koppal, Karnataka; management says it is operating as projected and a repeat order is possible.
Blades currently imported; localisation under way, with in-house blade manufacturing planned.
Ash handling capacity not a constraint per management; scaling depends on multiplying fleet and manpower. Working in 42 thermal power plants, about 30-35% of Indian TPPs.
Railway Rail-cum-Road (RCR) initiative started, with freight discounts opening Northeast routes.
demand_pricing: Ash handling realisation varies from INR450 to INR1,200 per tonne-km, driven mainly by distance and volume.
Ash handling order book INR1,635 crore; management says digital tender wins in the past four months should improve the Q4 order book.
Wind order book INR1,860 crore; management says large orders are expected this year, at least as big as last year.
Management welcomes new entrants in ash handling, arguing they expand awareness and market; says Refex is the only organised player.
Wind market tailwinds cited from hybrid renewables (wind, solar, storage) and the 100 GW by 2030 government ambition. Exports ruled out; focus is domestic only.

qa_highlights.question: What was the ash and coal handling volume run rate and the Q4 target?
qa_highlights.answer: 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1; target close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (also cited as crossing 75,000-80,000).

qa_highlights.question: Why is wind margin near zero in Q1 and what is the full-year margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operating and business development expenses were expensed; part of material is in transit and unbilled. Management targets 5-6% net margin (PAT) for the year, with better margins in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance for ash handling, given conflicting statements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it always guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%; Q1 EBITDA margin was 17%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind order book and outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: INR1,860 crore in hand, of which INR525 crore executed; INR1,300 crore to be executed in FY27. New orders would spill into FY28; growth expected to be very good, with no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pledge reduction trajectory for promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge was reduced last month, another disclosure due within 15 days, with further releases expected within two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind JV structure and technology arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Refex holds about 76-77%, the JV partner 23%; technology was transferred directly for payment, and the partner runs operations. Management did not disclose the partner's equity infusion on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is the mobility demerger affecting P&L and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Discontinued operations to end by Q3 FY27; the mobility entity will be listed separately via mirror shareholding. Capital allocation will be based on need, with wind capital requirements likely at entity level through working capital or term loans.

risks_watch: Diesel supply shortages and logistics disruptions from geopolitical developments affected operations; management said most of the impact was covered.
Wind segment margin only just breaks even in Q1; delivery of the 5-6% net margin target depends on Q3-Q4 billing of in-transit material.
Q2 FY27 volume seasonality in ash handling; ramp to 90,000 tonnes per day depends on fleet and manpower additions.
Mobility demerger approval steps (equity shareholder meeting next month, NCLT, creditors) and the timing of discontinued operation losses ending by Q3 FY27.
Blade localisation timeline (6-12 months) and the sustainability of margins at the wind plant; no replacement-blade orders yet.
Promoter pledge reduction ongoing; management plans further disclosures in about 15 days.
Management gave inconsistent statements on wind margin basis (net vs PAT) and on Q4 run rate targets, which should be clarified in the next filing.

Yes, it is a net margin, Sudhir bhai.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the core ash and coal handling business and on the wind ramp, with specific numbers on revenue, EBITDA and order book. Noticeably cautious and vague on wind margin basis, the Q4 run-rate target (90,000 vs 75,000-80,000 tonnes per day), promoter pledge and JV partner equity, where management deferred to earlier disclosures or gave no figure.
